whatis.intro: Markup is the amount you add to a cost to set a price, written as a share of that cost. It is a rule for reaching a price, not the share of the price you keep.

cards.title: What it is measured on
cards.body: What you paid, not what you charge. Because the base is the cost, a markup can run past 100%, while a margin never reaches it.
cards.alt: Open book, for the cost a markup is measured on

cards.title: Markup on cost, markup on retail
cards.body: Distributors usually state markup on cost. Retail pricing often states it on the selling price instead, so a store buyer's 40% may already be a margin.
cards.alt: Warning sign, for the two ways the trade states a markup

cards.title: Why the trade keeps using it
cards.body: It is one multiplication on a number you already know. Cost times 1.40 prices a $22.00 case at $30.80 on the spot. Hitting a margin takes a division instead.
cards.alt: Light bulb, for pricing a case with one multiplication

who.intro: Pricing teams at distributors that work from a cost sheet use it to turn a markup into a price and a margin. Anyone who sets a markup, translates a buyer's percentage or checks a price list should run it.

look.h2: Before you pick a markup rung
look.intro: The ladder is exact arithmetic. What goes wrong is the cost you start from and the target you aim at.

steps.title: A cost for the unit you sell
steps.body: If you split cases and sell eaches, divide the $22.00 by the pack before you mark it up. A rung on the case cost does not price a single each.

steps.title: A gross target, not a net one
steps.body: The 30% target is gross margin, before delivery, sales pay and rent. Type the net margin you hope to keep and the markup comes out far too low.

steps.title: Price endings that round up
steps.body: If your list rounds prices to set endings, round $31.43 up, not down. Rounding down to the nearest ending puts the case under its target.

vos.h2: Where VOS fits next to the ladder
vos.h3: The orders behind your case counts
vos.body: VOS does not calculate markups or set prices. It touches one input, the case count behind your monthly gross profit. Every order a customer speaks into the VOS app is saved to that account's history, in one admin platform.
bullets: Each app order carries a number, date and timestamp
Order guides updated in the same place when a price moves
Each account orders at the prices you set, tied to your SKUs
